name: Dandenong Market

facts.claim: Retail market at the corner of Clow and Cleeland Streets in Dandenong, established in 1866
More than 200 traders across about 8,000 square metres, from fresh produce and deli to the Bazaar of general merchandise

access_note: Open only Fri-Sun per official site (affects 'there whenever a visitor arrives'; bio should say so). Entry free, no fee page; open vs entry basis for orchestrator.

name: Capital City Trail

facts.claim: Shared-use path about 29 km long circling Melbourne's city centre and inner northern and eastern suburbs
Mostly made of sections of other trails: Merri Creek, Main Yarra, Moonee Ponds Creek and Inner Circle Rail Trail
Easy, sealed surface; popular start at Princes Bridge near Flinders Street station

ticketUrl_note: no single steward (path of several councils/agencies)

name: Yarra Bend Park

facts.claim: Melbourne's largest natural bushland park, on the Yarra River
Grey-headed flying-foxes roost in the park, with a walking trail and viewing platform from Bellbird Picnic Area
Dights Falls, a weir built in the 1840s for the Ceres flour mill, is its best-known feature
Canoes can be hired at Studley Park Boathouse

name: Warrandyte State Park

facts.claim: Closest state park to Melbourne, 24 km north-east of the city along the Yarra River
Pound Bend picnic area with a 2.4 km return river walk where eastern grey kangaroos are often seen
Gold-mining relics at Pound Bend, Fourth Hill and Black Flat, including the Evelyn Tunnel
Mount Lofty Circuit Walk (4.7 km) climbs to the park's highest point with views over the Yarra Valley

name: Organ Pipes National Park

facts.claim: Basalt columns resembling organ pipes hang over Jacksons Creek, formed about a million years ago from lava from volcanoes near Sunbury
Also features Rosette Rock and the Tessellated Pavement, a mosaic-like basalt outcrop
Only access is a short, steep bitumen path down from the car park on an old volcano
